Rationale.Paragraph: Why the renderer owns every GUI-visible string and Rust only a structured fact: the rollback facts originate inside m068, but the user-facing voice already lives in the ten-locale store (the rollback card itself is localized — the store's hardcoded English was the outlier, finding 14). Letting Rust errors reach the GUI raw is exactly the defect; duplicating locale machinery into Rust would create a second translation surface for one notice. The constraint that Rust changes only by the additive fact channel also protects the deferred work: the four rollback-integrity defects stay deferred precisely because no restore logic is reopened here.

Why a persisted marker plus a read-and-clear command, not an event: the GUI restore ends by restarting the process (macOS) or spawning the installer and exiting (Windows) — any in-memory event dies with the process it was emitted on, and the audience of the prefs-skip fact is the NEXT session, a fresh process. A bounded JSON marker (restore-outcome.json) at the rollback root itself — never inside the live/ set, which the restore's own remove_dir_all and the boot finalization both delete — is the minimal fact that survives the restart; its error field is capped at 200 chars so the bounded-schema promise survives future error-chain changes; read-and-clear makes the notice one-shot by construction; removing a stale marker at every restore entry (GUI and CLI) and any unconsumed marker at the prepare entry keeps the same era clean; and the marker's at timestamp bounds the fact absolutely — the renderer consumer suppresses anything older than 48 h with a console marker only — which is what closes the transition era, where the restored pre-feature binary's own prepare cannot know the marker and the next new binary's first boot would otherwise inherit a weeks-old skip. The skip site itself is the macOS-only logged-and-skipped path (a Windows prefs failure hard-aborts the restore and surfaces through the localized restore-failure notice instead).

Why registering the command is a four-site chain: the Rust allowlist (REGISTERED_COMMANDS) and the embedded tauri.v2.json fixture are enforced by the boot parity gate (drift exits 1 in either direction); the generate_handler! registration is hand-synced per the m001 MODULE_CONTRACT; and the ipc-contract types cover the fixture transitively (the gen tool derives it from the CommandMap) — so an additive command is only additive when all four sites move together (the fixture regenerated by the repo's own gen tool, never hand-written; the two non-gated sites are pinned by the plan's TargetAssertions, and the command carries the app-store stub variant the m068 cluster's pattern requires).

Why the card stays hidden and a notice carries failure (the spec's "keeps the card OR raises an error notification"): the failure moment on macOS may be immediately followed by a successful restore-and-restart that is already in flight — resurrecting a confirmation dialog for an operation that may be completing anyway would lie to the user. The warning notice is honest, non-blocking, and matches the accepted notification voice; the card-hiding order (visible = false before the attempt) is unchanged and recorded as the plan's interpretation. Severities follow the spec's literal words: the restore-failure notice is error severity (which the store's own rule makes sticky — a confirmed-but-failed rollback must not vanish), while the prefs-skip notice is a sticky warning (an unpinned warning auto-dismisses in 10 s, and the read-and-clear fact can never resurface — a one-shot fact deserves a one-chance read).

Why copy failure stays silent but truthful: the owner-accepted M-067 voice made selection-copy a quiet developer feature — "no toast about a toast" (C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM R-3). Finding 13 was never the silence; it was the FALSE SUCCESS pulse. So copySelectionText keeps the silent-failure contract but stops reporting success it did not observe, and the pulse becomes conditional on the real outcome. Nothing about the silence changes for the user; everything about the lie changes.

Why the CLI stderr human lines stay English (the plan's interpretation of "the strings C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES added"): those strings live in the pre-boot --rollback CLI path — a developer surface with an audience of one, where R-8's ten-locale notice rule does not reach and dragging locale tables into Rust would buy nothing. They reach GUI users today only as raw invoke errors through the finding-14 surface — and this change stops showing raw invoke errors in the GUI, which retires the actual debt; their English lives on in CLI output and logs where it belongs.

Why the action-failure notice is generic rather than reveal-specific: the card's action set is open (handler or payload, any kind); the only rejecting actions today are the two Reveal payloads, but the honest contract is outcome-truth for any action. A quiet generic copy (notifications.actionFailedTitle/Body) covers future actions without per-kind keys, and the raw error stays in the console marker for diagnosis.

Why this wave lands strictly after C-STATS-READOUT: the two graph/verification files are shared with that change's T-007 (both amend features.xml and verification/features.xml). Serial ordering — rebase this branch once the sibling's deltas land — is cheaper and safer than merging XML deltas from parallel branches; the parallel-preflight overlap on those files is honored as a sequencing rule, not disputed.

Alternatives.Alternative: Localize the Rust human lines in place: rejected — locale machinery inside the Rust CLI for a developer surface, duplicating the renderer's ten-locale tables; the GUI debt is retired by stopping raw-error display instead.

Keep the confirmation card visible on restore failure: rejected — the restore may already be completing toward a restart; a resurrected dialog can contradict reality within seconds; the notice is the honest voice.
A toast/notice on copy failure: rejected — the owner-accepted quiet-developer voice for selection-copy; the defect was the false success pulse, not the silence.
A Tauri event emit as the fact channel: rejected — the emitting process is the one the restore terminates; events cannot cross the restart that the fact must survive.

Extending mt_rollback_status with an outcome field: rejected — status gates the rollback card's presence; overloading it couples the boot card logic with the one-shot notice; a dedicated read-and-clear command keeps each surface single-purpose and self-clearing.

A renderer-written localStorage marker before invoking the restore: rejected — the renderer never learns the outcome; only Rust performs the restore and the restart, so only Rust can record the truth.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Localizing the CLI human lines (ten locales in stderr) — deferred unless the pre-boot --rollback path ever grows a non-developer audience.
Any feedback for the notificationsHistory copy action (today plain copy, no pulse) — deferred; this change only makes its return-value consumption explicit and unchanged.

The pre-existing silent failure of OPEN_ROLLBACK_CONFIRM's status query (autoUpdates.js:309-312, console-only, no notice) — a candidate for the deferred feedback-hygiene sweep; out of scope here per the spec's NonGoals.

A sweep of other legacy hardcoded English notice strings outside the rollback surface — a separate localization-hygiene change; this wave owns its keys only (the seven it defines, including the source-chip key that already rendered raw on the rollback card).
Collapsing simultaneous failures into one combined notice — deferred; each surface (action, restore, copy, boot) reports independently today and the cases barely coincide.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reveal fails (volume unmounted between export and click): the awaited payload rejects, the card shows the localized action-failed warning once, the console marker carries the platform error, nothing is unhandled — at both editor.js call sites.

The dynamic import of @tauri-apps/api/core fails at confirm time (the finding-12 hole): the rejection lands in the catch, the localized restore-failed notice replaces the old silence-and-vanish, the component's awaited promise settles quietly.

Clipboard blocked (permissions or missing API): copySelectionText resolves false on both copy-on-select surfaces (card and editor banner), with the Range captured synchronously so a collapsed selection can neither throw past the handler nor pulse the wrong node — no pulse fires, no notice appears; the user simply sees no confirmation, which is now the truth.

Rollback completed but preferences restore skipped: the restored session boots, the outcome query (which precedes the updater gate, so a throttled or disabled check cannot suppress it) returns the record, the localized sticky prefs-skipped warning appears exactly once; the next boot is silent; the CLI stderr line still names the reason for the developer.
A stale restore-outcome.json from an abandoned cycle: the next restore that actually starts removes it before any write — it can never surface after an unrelated future update.

A locale table missing one of the seven keys at runtime: the i18n layer's existing fallback path applies exactly as for any other key; the locale-keys gate makes shipping such a table a test failure, not a runtime surprise.
